Okay, so I'm trying to figure out why watering plants and grass in the early morning is a way to conserve water. The options given are A, B, C, and D. I need to determine which one is correct. Let me break this down step by step.

First, I know that water is a precious resource, so finding ways to use it efficiently is important. Watering in the morning seems counterintuitive because sometimes it's cooler then, but I'm not sure how that helps conserve water. Maybe it has something to do with evaporation.

Option A says there's always more water in the morning. Hmm, I'm not sure about that. I think the amount of water in the morning might depend on the season or the area. It might be more in some places but not others. Plus, if it's a dry area, the morning might not have more water. So maybe A isn't correct.

Option B states that smaller amounts of water evaporate in the cool morning. Evaporation is when water turns into vapor and goes into the air. I remember that hotter water evaporates faster. So if you water in the morning when it's cooler, less water would evaporate before it has a chance to be used by the plants. That makes sense because it would prevent waste through evaporation and save water for when it's needed more, like in the afternoon when the sun is out and it's hotter.

Option C suggests that water used in the morning can be recycled for afternoon use. I'm not sure about this. Water used by plants isn't typically recycled back into the water supply system. It's more about the plants using it for growth. So maybe C isn't the right reason.

Option D says grass can absorb water only in the morning. I don't think that's true. Grass can absorb water any time of the day, as long as the soil isn't too dry. So D doesn't seem correct either.

Putting it all together, the most logical answer seems to be B. Watering in the morning uses less water because it doesn't evaporate as quickly, leaving more water available for other uses or for the plants to use throughout the day.
